solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Player, one dropping to secure laced boot

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so the faller wraps around the other letters

parts.note: a faller is one who falls, especially a horse that drops in a race

indicators.note: laced suggests the letters are threaded through and rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer, just after a fall, does up his boots.
explanation.walkthrough: A faller is racing jargon for a horse that falls; 'laced' makes OOTB, which 'to secure' wraps in.
explanation.definitionFit: A footballer is a person who plays the game of football, so a kind of player.

clue.text: Fashion house's finale, dull

parts.note: a fad is a passing fashion or craze

indicators.note: the finale of a word is its closing letter

explanation.surface: A fashion house's closing show turns out to be dull.
explanation.definitionFit: To dull is to lose brightness or colour, which is what fabric or light does as it weakens.

clue.text: Boat tour without limits set off

indicators.note: the word loses its first and last letters, its limits

parts.note: taken as written, then trimmed
to trigger something is to set it off

explanation.surface: A boat trip with no boundaries gets under way.
explanation.definitionFit: An outrigger is a canoe fitted with a float projecting from its side, a type of vessel.

clue.text: Vagrant embraced by massive drinker — almost touching, though not moving?

parts.note: a bumper crop or harvest is a massive one

indicators.note: being embraced means being held inside, so the vagrant goes within the drinker

parts.note: a toper is a heavy drinker
a bum is a vagrant or tramp

explanation.surface: A tramp is hugged by a huge drinker, close together but going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a traffic jam, where cars sit nose to tail without moving.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes queued cars so tightly packed they nearly touch, typically in a stationary traffic jam.

clue.text: Destiny, crowning glory for Holy Roman Emperor

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny
a person's hair is proverbially their crowning glory

explanation.surface: Fate and a fine head of hair suit an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Lothair I was a ninth-century Frankish ruler who held the title of emperor in the West.

clue.text: Does out old bearings

parts.note: ex means former or old, as in an ex-partner
a person's bearing is their posture, so poses are bearings

explanation.surface: Someone discovers the outdated ball bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: To out someone is to reveal a secret about them, which is to lay them bare publicly.

clue.text: A police department rotter?

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Is a member of the detective branch a cad?
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotter' looks like a cad, but here it means something that rots or corrodes; CID is the British plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A corrosive substance eats away at metal or tissue, so it is something that makes things decay.

clue.text: Vegetable left too long on the barbecue, did you say?

indicators.note: a question about what was spoken points to a word heard rather than read

parts.words: left too long on the barbecue
parts.note: food left too long over the coals is charred, burnt black

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether the vegetable was overdone on the grill.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard is a leafy green related to beet, eaten cooked like spinach.

clue.text: Exact replica phone cut off, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a telephone whose line has gone dead is a lifeless ringing device

explanation.surface: A perfect copy of a phone whose line has been cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is an idiom for someone or something that looks exactly like another.

clue.text: Niche I try at first, suitable for design of light bulb

parts.note: a bay is a recess or niche in a wall
the numeral I is one

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: fitting means appropriate or suitable

explanation.surface: Someone tries a wall recess for a lamp that seems to suit it.
explanation.walkthrough: A bayonet fitting is the push-and-twist cap common on British bulbs, as opposed to the screw type.
explanation.definitionFit: The bayonet cap, pushed in and turned to lock, is one standard way a bulb's base is made.

clue.text: A corporation beyond despicable at first — fact!

indicators.note: coming beyond something means placed after it
only the opening letter of the preceding word is taken

parts.note: corporation is old slang for a paunch, a big belly or tum

explanation.surface: A company is denounced as despicable, and that is a fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' looks like a business, but it is dated British slang for a pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A datum is a single piece of information, a given fact used as a basis for reasoning.

clue.text: Chief has to lead with three articles

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
the articles an, an and a run together

explanation.surface: The boss must take charge using three items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a verb for being in charge, but it is the metal, symbol Pb.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal slang for the most important person in a group, the boss.

clue.text: Win earned, synod wasted brief success

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined, so these letters are broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A church council's hard-won victory proves fleeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names something that causes a sensation for a short while and is soon forgotten.

clue.text: Modify harmony that sounds a work of art in church

definitions.text: a work of art in church

indicators.note: a phrase that sounds like something signals a word heard, not spelt

parts.note: modify means alter and harmony means peace, said together

explanation.surface: Changing the harmony produces an artwork that sounds well in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: An altarpiece is a painting or carving set above and behind a church's main table of worship.

clue.text: Boat carrying less cargo?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships
having a smaller load, so weighing less

explanation.surface: A vessel that holds less freight.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge that ferries goods ashore, and a less heavily loaded ship is less heavy.

clue.text: Fire this good behind a number of warmer houses

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside

parts.note: the sun is what warms the earth

indicators.note: being behind means coming after

parts.note: ten is a number

explanation.surface: An instruction to light this, rewarded by several cosy homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: a Sten gun is something you fire, a British submachine gun of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition reads as a command to shoot, and the weapon is a light automatic firearm.

clue.text: Furious loading keeps ship in rapid passage

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within
furious suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: Frantic loading of a vessel during a quick crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passage' is musical, not a voyage; 'Furious' makes GLIANDO, and 'keeps' holds the ship within.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a musical slide in which the player sweeps quickly through a run of notes.

clue.text: A European overshadowing British performer

indicators.note: to overshadow is to loom over and cover, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a Croat is a person from Croatia

explanation.surface: A continental act eclipses a home-grown one.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a circus or stage entertainer who does gymnastic feats.

clue.text: African city more stimulating for the epicurean?

definitions.meaning: a Moroccan port on the Strait of Gibraltar
having a sharper, zestier flavour, as a gourmet would put it

explanation.surface: A North African city that a gourmet finds more exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a port in Morocco, and food with more tang has a sharper, more piquant taste.

clue.text: Do I start to complain when hugged by bear briefly?

indicators.note: being hugged means being held inside, so these letters go within the other
a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: to bear something is to suffer it

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Should I begin moaning when a bear squeezes me?
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb to endure; SUFFER cut short gives SUFFE.
explanation.definitionFit: 'That will do' means that will be enough, so to do is to be adequate.

clue.text: Marine plant ending in trouble in river, was surfacing

indicators.note: in shows one letter set within the others
in a down entry, rising to the surface means reading upwards, from the end

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and another in Wales and England

indicators.note: only the final letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A seaweed caught up in trouble in a river came to the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'surfacing' means read upwards, giving SAWEED; 'in' then slips the final E of trouble inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaweed is the general name for algae growing in the sea, such as kelp or wrack.

clue.text: Might steps be taken to avoid one's work?

definitions.text: Might steps be taken to avoid one's work?

parts.words: Might steps be taken to avoid one's work?
parts.note: pedestrians step around chalk drawings on a pavement, so people literally take steps to avoid the work of this street artist

explanation.surface: It seems to ask whether someone dodges their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steps be taken to avoid' reads as shirking, but passers-by walk around chalk drawings on the pavement, British for sidewalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a street painter draws in chalk on the walkway, and passers-by step round the pictures.

clue.text: Uninspiring short film about a piano

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it
short means the word is cut down, here losing its ending

parts.note: a video is a recorded film
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

explanation.surface: A brief, dull movie about a piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Vapid means flat and lacking liveliness, so it offers nothing to stimulate.

clue.text: Sexual attraction beginning to evaporate with married couple

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: The spark of desire starts to fade for a husband and wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a romantic relationship are informally called an item.

clue.text: Telex VIP sent with English obscenity

indicators.note: sent here means sent flying, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: An important person dispatches a rude telex in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent' rearranges TELEXVIP into EXPLETIV, then E for English finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An expletive is a swear word, an oath or curse that may be crude.

clue.text: Tag question in potential source of irritation

parts.note: a nit, a louse egg, may make the scalp itch

explanation.surface: A tag asks whether something in the clothing might be itchy.
explanation.walkthrough: A tag question is the little query added to the end of a sentence; British slang 'innit' is a contraction of 'isn't it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Innit is colloquial British for isn't it, tacked onto a statement as a tag question.

clue.text: Somewhat revered, dark collection of legends

indicators.note: somewhat means a part of, so a few letters are taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A revered, rather dark book of myths.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddas are Old Norse works that preserve the myths and heroic poems of Scandinavia.

clue.text: Man United soon to control opening of game, sweeper claims

indicators.note: to claim something is to take hold of it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a broom is used for sweeping
to ride a horse is to control it

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Manchester United's sweeper says he'll soon take control of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man United' looks like the football club, but it is a man about to be united in marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridegroom is a man on his wedding day, shortly to be joined to his partner.
